title: The DRG normalization batch (census 948)

banner.title: The DRG normalization batch - the five Dragon magazine defs (death angel, mihalli, prowler, qu'uni, vriyagga) rewritten to the full-field 57-key emission
banner.provenance: The registry close - the per-book schema pass lands its last book (the R879 normalizer doctrine: MM1 R1009-R1014, the OA book R1016, the MM2 arc R1017-R1020, the FF arc R1021-R1023, the WSG+MOP tail R1024): the five The Dragon magazine variant-layer defs rewritten to the canonical FIELD_ORDER emission, byte-exact against the landed normalize_registry.py, and the registry closes 1338 of 1338 defs canonical - every def of the census carries the full-field emission; the first comma-site round of the arc - each DRG text field lacked the Lua-optional trailing comma, so each of the five end-of-body windows is one whole-line rewrite merged with the sentinel insert, no bare deletes shipped, the sweep green pre-handoff (member scan, value invariance, quote parity, brace balance, name and source invariance, normalizer exactness and idempotence, xp formula zero exceptions).

audit_comment: THE REGISTRY CLOSES - the five Dragon magazine defs (death angel, mihalli, prowler, qu'uni, vriyagga) rewritten to the full-field 57-key emission, byte-exact against the landed normalize_registry.py, the registry 1338 of 1338 canonical; thirty anchored sentinel inserts and the first five comma-site whole-line rewrites of the arc (the DRG text fields lacked the Lua-optional trailing comma).
include_after: #include "rules/wt1.h"  // R1024: the WSG+MOP normalization tail batch

file_patches.from:
text = "The Death Angel is a finger of Fate utilised by very powerful entities - gods, demi-gods, some liches and very few evil high priests of 20th level or higher. It acts as an Oracle warning of death or represents Death itself on a mission to kill one particular being; it attacks only its intended victim and leaves once the kill is made. Those successfully killed rise as Death Angels after three days unless raised - only Raise Dead Fully works (and then as a regular Raise Dead), the percent chance rolls as if constitution were 3, and a Wish works automatically; a being killed three times is gone forever. The only permanent dispelling is a remove curse thrown on a slain Death Angel battling its intended victim, granting eternal peace; there can be no more than one Death Angel serving any one master. The XP conversion rides the DMG p.85 additive formula - 225 base + 2 specials x 175 + 1 exceptional x 275, plus 8 per hit point at the floored 31 average (7 dice at 4.5 per die) - noted, never silent; promoted from The Dragon Vol. 1 No. 6 (April 1977), folio 29, as a variant-layer def."
}

file_patches.from:
text = "The Mihalli are humanoid, hermaphroditic shape-changers whose skins run from dull green in the lower forms to coppery brown in the higher; they see in the dark. They appear 1-20 near their own territory; 40 percent of the time their lair (80-800 gold) holds Eyes, amulets or scrolls. There is a 20 percent chance each turn they are looked at that their glowing red eyes reveal them. The higher Mihalli command at least two bonus spells, three-plus at levels IV and up. A friendly party is treated well - 5 percent per turn, rolled randomly, with a 1 percent chance of an offered magical item - and the Mihalli defends itself if attacked. The Ball of Immediate Eventuation climbs a four-step colour ladder from light purple through bright silver and bright gold to lambent translucent blue; its use is reserved to magic users and priests of the fourteenth level and up, and below that it scrambles brains. The print stat lines F: 50 and I: 50 garble in both the PDF layer and the OCR and ride pinned AS SCANNED; promoted from The Dragon Vol. 1 No. 4 (December 1976), folios 18-19, as a variant-layer def, the DMG p.85 XP conversion and the 4.5-per-die d8 average noted, never silent."
}

file_patches.from:
text = "The Prowler lays her eggs beneath the skin of the mind-blanked zombeis with the brown tentacles that line her mouth, dealing 1-8 however tenderly done; the zombeis wander 2-8 days until the eggs hatch and the baby prowlers make their host their first meal. Exceptionally intelligent prowlers form hatcheries - charming large numbers as guards and egg hosts in abandoned caves or underground. A zombei's mind is restored only by three Patriarchs simultaneously casting dispel evil. The XP conversion rides the DMG p.85 additive formula - 1800 base + 3 specials x 950 (the gaze, the constriction, the magic resistance) + 1 exceptional x 1200 (the hatchery lifecycle), plus 18 per hit point at the 63 average (14 dice at 4.5 per die) - noted, never silent; promoted from The Dragon Vol. I No. 7 (June 1977), folio 24, as a variant-layer def."
}

file_patches.from:
text = "The Vriyagga is a tentacled creature of the cities, 1-10 appearing, 20-200 in its own city, armor class 1, moving 12, 10 or 8 inches per turn by size with 10, 15 or 25 hit dice. It carries four or more tentacles, more in the larger forms; it takes armor class 2 to sever one, and a tentacle does 2, 4 or 6 dice of damage per turn by size. It senses heat, cannot speak, but thinks, organizes and lays ambushes; it cannot climb stairs. Its black-opal eyes see in the dark. Treasure is nil, even in lair. The def pins the 15-dice middle size for the XP formula; promoted from The Dragon Vol. 1 No. 4 (December 1976), folios 19 and 21, as a variant-layer def, the DMG p.85 XP conversion and the 4.5-per-die d8 average noted, never silent."
}
